All quasi-psh and psh potentials are genuine canonical upper representatives; arbitrary almost-everywhere modifications are excluded. A smooth real background theta is nef if theta+epsilon h has a strictly positive smooth dd^c-potential representative for every epsilon>0, where h is a fixed Hermitian metric; it is big if theta+dd^c u>=delta h for some delta>0 and genuine global quasi-psh u. For every smooth positive Gauduchon metric gamma with dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0 define D_mu(gamma)=integral (mu/gamma^n)^(1/n) gamma^n, lambda_mu(theta)=inf_gamma integral theta wedge gamma^(n-1)/D_mu(gamma), and V_mu(theta)=lambda_mu(theta)^n for nef theta, using decreasing epsilon-regularization at a nef boundary. Every Gauduchon metric participates. Use the normalized Chern-Ricci form Ric(omega)=-dd^c log omega^n and Chern-Ricci flow partial_t omega(t)=-Ric(omega(t)); time rescales if another convention is used. Assume a smooth Hermitian initial metric omega_0, finite maximal time tau, and the nef limiting background theta_tau=omega_0-tau Ric(omega_0). Differentiating the defining flux gives A_ε^m/ω^m=1/[H_ε(a+ε)]. At x=0, q_ε is x times a smooth positive function; at x=1, q_ε(1)=1. These facts remove both apparent singularities of φ_ε′. The variational lower bound applies to every smooth positive Gauduchon metric. For S=γ^(n−1), distributional Stokes gives ∫θ∧S=∫Ω∧S. Off Z, matrix AM–GM gives Ω∧S≥n^(1/n)(μ/γ^n)^(1/n)γ^n. Since θ≤θ_ε and c_ε→n, the endpoint infimum is exactly n^(1/n). notes.text:
Independent proof of every target A, for every integer m≥2 and n=m+1.

Pullbacks to X=P^m×P^1 are suppressed. With dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂, the normalized Fubini–Study form on Z0≠0 is omega=dd^c log(1+|z|²), z=(Z1/Z0,…,Zm/Z0). Write r=|z|² and x=r/(1+r). Globally, x=Σ_{j=1}^m|Zj|²/Σ_{j=0}^m|Zj|² is smooth, takes values in [0,1], and vanishes exactly at p=[1:0:…:0]. Set beta=(m-1)/m, a=x/beta, h=omega+w, and mu=omega^m∧w. The product is connected and compact, h is smooth positive, and mu is a smooth strictly positive probability volume.

Polar normalization. For an integrable radial function F,

∫_{P^m}F(x)omega^m=m∫_0^1 F(y)y^{m-1}dy.

Indeed the affine Hessian determinant of log(1+r) is (1+r)^(-m-1), so omega^m=(m!/π^m)(1+r)^(-m-1)dVol_{R^{2m}}. Angular integration gives dVol=(π^m/(m-1)!)r^{m-1}dr. Substitution x=r/(1+r) gives m x^{m-1}dx. The omitted projective hyperplane has zero smooth volume. This proves ∫omega^m=1; the dimension-one calculation proves ∫w=1.

Radial Hessian. For F(r)=log(1+r)+v(x), define

q(x)=rF'(r)=x+x(1-x)v'(x).

The Hessian has transverse eigenvalue F'=q/r, with multiplicity m-1, and radial eigenvalue F'+rF''=q'(x)(1-x)². Relative to omega, their values are q/x and q'. Consequently

(omega+dd^c v)^m/omega^m=(q/x)^(m-1)q'

on 0<x<1.

Explicit smooth approximants. For epsilon>0 put b_epsilon=x/beta+epsilon and define

H_epsilon=m∫_0^1 y^{m-1}/(y/beta+epsilon)dy,
q_epsilon(x)^m=(m/H_epsilon)∫_0^x y^{m-1}/(y/beta+epsilon)dy,
phi_epsilon(x)=∫_0^x (q_epsilon(y)-y)/[y(1-y)]dy.

These are explicit scalar integrations, with no imported PDE existence theorem. H_epsilon>0 and q_epsilon(1)=1. Moreover

q_epsilon(x)/x=[(m/H_epsilon)∫_0^1 t^{m-1}/(xt/beta+epsilon)dt]^(1/m).

The bracket is smooth and strictly positive on a neighborhood of [0,1]. Thus q_epsilon/x extends smoothly and positively at zero. The numerator q_epsilon-x vanishes at zero and at one, so its quotient by x(1-x) extends smoothly at both endpoints. Therefore phi_epsilon is a global smooth function of x on P^m.

Differentiating gives

q_epsilon'=x^{m-1}/[H_epsilon b_epsilon q_epsilon^{m-1}]>0,
A_epsilon^m/omega^m=1/(H_epsilon b_epsilon),
A_epsilon=omega+dd^c phi_epsilon.

At zero the two relative eigenvalues q_epsilon/x and q_epsilon' have the same positive limit (H_epsilon epsilon)^(-1/m), proving smooth strict positivity at p.

Every other projective chart is checked as follows. On Zj≠0, j∈{1,…,m}, use zeta0=Z0/Zj and zetak=Zk/Zj for k≠0,j, and put S=1+Σ_{k≠0,j}|zetak|². Then x=S/(S+|zeta0|²) and omega=dd^c log(S+|zeta0|²). At zeta0=0 the local potential has expansion

log(S+|zeta0|²)+phi_epsilon(x)
=log S+phi_epsilon(1)+q_epsilon'(1)|zeta0|²/S+O(|zeta0|^4),

because phi_epsilon'(1)=1-q_epsilon'(1). Its tangential Hessian is positive Fubini–Study, its normal coefficient is q_epsilon'(1)/S>0, and mixed entries vanish there. Hence A_epsilon is smooth strictly positive on the hyperplane as well, and its volume formula extends there. In particular q_epsilon'(1)=1/[H_epsilon(1/beta+epsilon)]. This checks every base chart. The two reciprocal P^1 charts have the usual smooth expressions w=dd^c log(1+|eta|²) and w=dd^c log(1+|eta'|²), so all product forms below are global on both charts.

The limiting potential and its genuine representative. Monotone convergence gives

H_epsilon ↑ m beta∫_0^1 y^{m-2}dy=m beta/(m-1)=1

as epsilon↓0; m≥2 ensures integrability at zero. For each x>0, q_epsilon(x)^m→x^{m-1}, so q_epsilon(x)→x^beta. Thus the limiting potential is exactly

phi(x)=∫_0^x (y^beta-y)/[y(1-y)]dy.

Its derivative is O(y^(beta-1)) at zero and tends to 1-beta at one. It is nonnegative on (0,1). Therefore phi is bounded continuous with phi(0)=0, and smooth on (0,1] including as a function of x near one.

Uniform convergence fixes the canonical representative without any almost-everywhere modification. For 0<epsilon≤1, H_epsilon≥H_1>0 and q_epsilon≤H_1^(-1/m)x^beta. Also q_epsilon≥x: the displayed formula for q_epsilon/x is at least its value at x=1, which is 1. On x≤1/2 these bounds dominate |phi_epsilon'| by Cx^(beta-1). On x≥1/2 the formula for q_epsilon', together with q_epsilon≥x, H_epsilon≥H_1, and b_epsilon≥x/beta, gives a uniform derivative bound. Since q_epsilon(1)-1=0, it follows that |q_epsilon-x|≤C(1-x), and phi_epsilon' is uniformly bounded there. Dominated convergence proves ∫_0^1|phi_epsilon'-phi'|dx→0. As both potentials vanish at zero, phi_epsilon→phi uniformly.

In each local omega-potential chart, the smooth local potential plus phi_epsilon is psh. Its uniform limit is continuous psh, since upper semicontinuity and submean inequalities pass to the uniform limit. Hence phi is a genuine continuous omega-psh function, with its actual canonical value phi(p)=0. A=omega+dd^c phi is a globally positive closed current. It is also the distributional limit of A_epsilon.

Off p, inserting q=x^beta gives relative eigenvalues x^(beta-1), with multiplicity m-1, and beta x^(beta-1). Thus

A^m/omega^m=beta x^{m(beta-1)}=beta/x=1/a.

At x=1, phi'(1)=1-beta, and the same chart expansion gives tangential eigenvalues 1 and normal eigenvalue beta. Therefore A is smooth strictly positive everywhere off p, including the hyperplane, and the volume identity holds there too. Only smooth wedges off p are used; no global singular Monge–Ampère wedge is needed.

Nefness, nonclosedness, and nonbigness. The smooth form theta=omega+a w is semipositive. For every epsilon>0,

theta+epsilon h=(1+epsilon)omega+(a+epsilon)w>0,

so theta is nef in the prescribed definition. Since dtheta=da∧w is nonzero where da≠0, it is genuinely nonclosed.

To obstruct bigness for every genuine global quasi-psh potential, let chi be a smooth nonnegative base function, pulled back to X. The smooth strongly semipositive (m,m) test chi omega^m satisfies dd^c(chi omega^m)=0: omega is closed, and dd^c chi∧omega^m vanishes by horizontal dimension. For any scalar distribution u, distributional Stokes gives ∫dd^c u∧chi omega^m=0. If theta+dd^c u≥delta h for delta>0, positivity would imply

0≤∫_X(theta+dd^c u-delta h)∧chi omega^m
=∫_{P^m}(a-delta)chi omega^m.

Choose nonzero chi supported in the open set a<delta, which exists because a(p)=0. The integral is strictly negative, a contradiction. This includes all genuine quasi-psh u, even those equal to minus infinity on the fiber over p. It never restricts a singular potential to a fiber and uses no nonclosed product mass identity.

Exact infimum over all Gauduchon metrics. Prove the more general formula for k>0:

Theta_{k,epsilon}=k omega+b_epsilon w,
B_{k,epsilon}=k A_epsilon+b_epsilon w=Theta_{k,epsilon}+dd^c(k phi_epsilon).

Both are smooth strictly positive, and

B_{k,epsilon}^n=n k^m b_epsilon A_epsilon^m∧w=C mu,
C=n k^m/H_epsilon.

For ANY smooth positive Gauduchon gamma, dd^c gamma^m=0. Stokes gives equality of the integrated pairings of Theta and B. Matrix AM–GM gives pointwise

B∧gamma^m=(tr(gamma^(-1)B)/n)gamma^n
≥(B^n/gamma^n)^(1/n)gamma^n
=C^(1/n)(mu/gamma^n)^(1/n)gamma^n.

Thus the defining quotient is at least C^(1/n) for every participating Gauduchon metric; no restriction to invariant or product tests has been made.

For actual attainment define

gamma_{k,epsilon}=b_epsilon^(-1/m)B_{k,epsilon}.

It is a global smooth positive metric, and

gamma_{k,epsilon}^m=b_epsilon^(-1)k^m A_epsilon^m+m k^{m-1}A_epsilon^{m-1}∧w.

The first term is pulled back from a top-degree base form and therefore d-closed; the second is a product of closed forms. Hence gamma is Gauduchon, in fact balanced. It is conformal to B, so AM–GM is an equality. Directly,

gamma^n=C b_epsilon^(-n/m)mu,
∫Theta∧gamma^m=C∫b_epsilon^(-1)mu=C H_epsilon=n k^m,
D_mu(gamma)=C^(m/n)H_epsilon.

The quotient is C^(1/n), proving

lambda_mu(Theta_{k,epsilon})^n=n k^m/H_epsilon.

For k=1 this gives all stated theta_epsilon formulas and actual smooth minimizing metrics. For k=1+epsilon it gives the exact Hermitian regularization value

lambda_mu(theta+epsilon h)^n=n(1+epsilon)^m/H_epsilon,

which decreases to n as epsilon decreases to zero.

The literal endpoint all-test infimum agrees. The positive current B_0=A+a w equals theta+dd^c phi. For every smooth positive Gauduchon gamma, Stokes and positivity give

∫theta∧gamma^m=∫B_0∧gamma^m
≥∫_{X\({p}×P^1)}B_0∧gamma^m
≥n^(1/n)D_mu(gamma).

On this complement, B_0 is smooth positive and B_0^n=n mu, so the preceding matrix inequality applies. The omitted fiber has zero mass for the smooth density appearing in D_mu. B_0∧gamma^m is a well-defined positive measure: it is a current wedged with a smooth form. No undefined singular determinant is used. Conversely theta≤theta_epsilon implies lambda_mu(theta)≤lambda_mu(theta_epsilon)=(n/H_epsilon)^(1/n). Taking epsilon↓0 proves

lambda_mu(theta)=n^(1/n), V_mu(theta)=n.

This is also the value obtained by the required decreasing Hermitian regularization. No smooth endpoint attaining metric is used or claimed.

Diagnostic evidence and limitations. checks.py symbolically verifies the radial eigenvalues and beta/x determinant. For m=2 it independently verifies phi(x)=2log(1+sqrt(x)). It compares H quadrature with the polynomial-division expression

H_epsilon=m beta[Σ_{j=0}^{m-2}(-c)^j/(m-1-j)+(-c)^(m-1)log((1+c)/c)], c=beta epsilon,

and checks the radial density using numerical differentiation. The successful run covers m=2,3,4,5,8,12 and epsilon=1,0.1,10^(-6): 18 parameter pairs, 54 pointwise density checks, and both minimizing quotient formulas. Its output reports PASS and maximum checked absolute algebra/quadrature error 3.4121697×10^(-39). For m=2, epsilon=1 it reports H=0.450693855665945154, V(theta_epsilon)=6.65640314880086523, and V(theta+epsilon h)=26.6256125952034609.

An initial unsplit 50-digit quadrature differed from the exact polynomial expression by about 5.06×10^(-33) at m=5, epsilon=10^(-6), exceeding the chosen tolerance. A single split still differed by 2.36×10^(-33); geometric splits at c,10c,100c,… resolved the numerical issue. The failure history is retained in checks.first.out and sources/check_history.txt. These are finite diagnostic observations, not exhaustive verification or substitutes for the proof valid for every m≥2.

notes.text:
Actual finite-time flow and its exact endpoint: target B.

Use the construction independently proved in n2. The initial metric

omega0=(n+1)omega+(a+2)w

is global smooth strictly positive, since n+1>0 and a+2≥2.

Its determinant and normalized Ricci form are exact. The product expansion gives

omega0^n=n(n+1)^m(a+2)mu.

The affine Fubini–Study determinant on P^m is a constant times (1+|z|²)^(-m-1), so -dd^c log omega^m=(m+1)omega=n omega. On P^1 the corresponding form is 2w. Coordinate changes contribute only pluriharmonic logarithms. Consequently

Ric(omega0)=n omega+2w-dd^c log(a+2),
alpha_t=omega0-t Ric(omega0)
=(n+1-nt)omega+(a+2-2t)w+t dd^c log(a+2).

For every 0≤t<1 the global smooth potential -t log(a+2) gives

alpha_t+dd^c[-t log(a+2)]
=(n+1-nt)omega+(a+2-2t)w>0.

Its horizontal coefficient exceeds 1, and its vertical coefficient is at least 2(1-t)>0. At t=1,

alpha1=theta+dd^c log(a+2).

This is a smooth gauge equivalence. It shows nefness using the strictly positive representatives of theta+epsilon h. It also shows nonbigness: a strict alpha1 representative would give a strict theta representative by adding the smooth function log(a+2) to its genuine quasi-psh potential, contradicting n2. Smooth addition preserves the canonical quasi-psh representative.

For every t>1 there is no positive current representative, including one obtained from an arbitrary scalar distribution u. Suppose alpha_t+dd^c u were positive. For a smooth nonnegative base function chi, the strongly semipositive test chi omega^m is dd^c-closed, as established in n2. Distributional Stokes removes dd^c u. The horizontal dd^c log(a+2) term has zero wedge with omega^m. Thus

notes.text:
Independent proof of every target A, for every integer m≥2 and n=m+1.

Pullbacks to X=P^m×P^1 are suppressed. With dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂, the normalized Fubini–Study form on Z0≠0 is omega=dd^c log(1+|z|²), z=(Z1/Z0,…,Zm/Z0). Write r=|z|² and x=r/(1+r). Globally, x=Σ_{j=1}^m|Zj|²/Σ_{j=0}^m|Zj|² is smooth, takes values in [0,1], and vanishes exactly at p=[1:0:…:0]. Set beta=(m-1)/m, a=x/beta, h=omega+w, and mu=omega^m∧w. The product is connected and compact, h is smooth positive, and mu is a smooth strictly positive probability volume.

Polar normalization. For an integrable radial function F,

∫_{P^m}F(x)omega^m=m∫_0^1 F(y)y^{m-1}dy.

Indeed the affine Hessian determinant of log(1+r) is (1+r)^(-m-1), so omega^m=(m!/π^m)(1+r)^(-m-1)dVol_{R^{2m}}. Angular integration gives dVol=(π^m/(m-1)!)r^{m-1}dr. Substitution x=r/(1+r) gives m x^{m-1}dx. The omitted projective hyperplane has zero smooth volume. This proves ∫omega^m=1; the dimension-one calculation proves ∫w=1.

Radial Hessian. For F(r)=log(1+r)+v(x), define

q(x)=rF'(r)=x+x(1-x)v'(x).

The Hessian has transverse eigenvalue F'=q/r, with multiplicity m-1, and radial eigenvalue F'+rF''=q'(x)(1-x)². Relative to omega, their values are q/x and q'. Consequently

(omega+dd^c v)^m/omega^m=(q/x)^(m-1)q'

on 0<x<1.

Explicit smooth approximants. For epsilon>0 put b_epsilon=x/beta+epsilon and define

H_epsilon=m∫_0^1 y^{m-1}/(y/beta+epsilon)dy,
q_epsilon(x)^m=(m/H_epsilon)∫_0^x y^{m-1}/(y/beta+epsilon)dy,
phi_epsilon(x)=∫_0^x (q_epsilon(y)-y)/[y(1-y)]dy.

These are explicit scalar integrations, with no imported PDE existence theorem. H_epsilon>0 and q_epsilon(1)=1. Moreover

q_epsilon(x)/x=[(m/H_epsilon)∫_0^1 t^{m-1}/(xt/beta+epsilon)dt]^(1/m).

The bracket is smooth and strictly positive on a neighborhood of [0,1]. Thus q_epsilon/x extends smoothly and positively at zero. The numerator q_epsilon-x vanishes at zero and at one, so its quotient by x(1-x) extends smoothly at both endpoints. Therefore phi_epsilon is a global smooth function of x on P^m.

Differentiating gives

q_epsilon'=x^{m-1}/[H_epsilon b_epsilon q_epsilon^{m-1}]>0,
A_epsilon^m/omega^m=1/(H_epsilon b_epsilon),
A_epsilon=omega+dd^c phi_epsilon.

At zero the two relative eigenvalues q_epsilon/x and q_epsilon' have the same positive limit (H_epsilon epsilon)^(-1/m), proving smooth strict positivity at p.

Every other projective chart is checked as follows. On Zj≠0, j∈{1,…,m}, use zeta0=Z0/Zj and zetak=Zk/Zj for k≠0,j, and put S=1+Σ_{k≠0,j}|zetak|². Then x=S/(S+|zeta0|²) and omega=dd^c log(S+|zeta0|²). At zeta0=0 the local potential has expansion

log(S+|zeta0|²)+phi_epsilon(x)
=log S+phi_epsilon(1)+q_epsilon'(1)|zeta0|²/S+O(|zeta0|^4),

because phi_epsilon'(1)=1-q_epsilon'(1). Its tangential Hessian is positive Fubini–Study, its normal coefficient is q_epsilon'(1)/S>0, and mixed entries vanish there. Hence A_epsilon is smooth strictly positive on the hyperplane as well, and its volume formula extends there. In particular q_epsilon'(1)=1/[H_epsilon(1/beta+epsilon)]. This checks every base chart. The two reciprocal P^1 charts have the usual smooth expressions w=dd^c log(1+|eta|²) and w=dd^c log(1+|eta'|²), so all product forms below are global on both charts.

The limiting potential and its genuine representative. Monotone convergence gives

H_epsilon ↑ m beta∫_0^1 y^{m-2}dy=m beta/(m-1)=1

as epsilon↓0; m≥2 ensures integrability at zero. For each x>0, q_epsilon(x)^m→x^{m-1}, so q_epsilon(x)→x^beta. Thus the limiting potential is exactly

phi(x)=∫_0^x (y^beta-y)/[y(1-y)]dy.

Its derivative is O(y^(beta-1)) at zero and tends to 1-beta at one. It is nonnegative on (0,1). Therefore phi is bounded continuous with phi(0)=0, and smooth on (0,1] including as a function of x near one.

Uniform convergence fixes the canonical representative without any almost-everywhere modification. For 0<epsilon≤1, H_epsilon≥H_1>0 and q_epsilon≤H_1^(-1/m)x^beta. Also q_epsilon≥x: the displayed formula for q_epsilon/x is at least its value at x=1, which is 1. On x≤1/2 these bounds dominate |phi_epsilon'| by Cx^(beta-1). On x≥1/2 the formula for q_epsilon', together with q_epsilon≥x, H_epsilon≥H_1, and b_epsilon≥x/beta, gives a uniform derivative bound. Since q_epsilon(1)-1=0, it follows that |q_epsilon-x|≤C(1-x), and phi_epsilon' is uniformly bounded there. Dominated convergence proves ∫_0^1|phi_epsilon'-phi'|dx→0. As both potentials vanish at zero, phi_epsilon→phi uniformly.

In each local omega-potential chart, the smooth local potential plus phi_epsilon is psh. Its uniform limit is continuous psh, since upper semicontinuity and submean inequalities pass to the uniform limit. Hence phi is a genuine continuous omega-psh function, with its actual canonical value phi(p)=0. A=omega+dd^c phi is a globally positive closed current. It is also the distributional limit of A_epsilon.

Off p, inserting q=x^beta gives relative eigenvalues x^(beta-1), with multiplicity m-1, and beta x^(beta-1). Thus

A^m/omega^m=beta x^{m(beta-1)}=beta/x=1/a.

At x=1, phi'(1)=1-beta, and the same chart expansion gives tangential eigenvalues 1 and normal eigenvalue beta. Therefore A is smooth strictly positive everywhere off p, including the hyperplane, and the volume identity holds there too. Only smooth wedges off p are used; no global singular Monge–Ampère wedge is needed.

Nefness, nonclosedness, and nonbigness. The smooth form theta=omega+a w is semipositive. For every epsilon>0,

theta+epsilon h=(1+epsilon)omega+(a+epsilon)w>0,

so theta is nef in the prescribed definition. Since dtheta=da∧w is nonzero where da≠0, it is genuinely nonclosed.

To obstruct bigness for every genuine global quasi-psh potential, let chi be a smooth nonnegative base function, pulled back to X. The smooth strongly semipositive (m,m) test chi omega^m satisfies dd^c(chi omega^m)=0: omega is closed, and dd^c chi∧omega^m vanishes by horizontal dimension. For any scalar distribution u, distributional Stokes gives ∫dd^c u∧chi omega^m=0. If theta+dd^c u≥delta h for delta>0, positivity would imply

0≤∫_X(theta+dd^c u-delta h)∧chi omega^m
=∫_{P^m}(a-delta)chi omega^m.

Choose nonzero chi supported in the open set a<delta, which exists because a(p)=0. The integral is strictly negative, a contradiction. This includes all genuine quasi-psh u, even those equal to minus infinity on the fiber over p. It never restricts a singular potential to a fiber and uses no nonclosed product mass identity.

Exact infimum over all Gauduchon metrics. Prove the more general formula for k>0:

Theta_{k,epsilon}=k omega+b_epsilon w,
B_{k,epsilon}=k A_epsilon+b_epsilon w=Theta_{k,epsilon}+dd^c(k phi_epsilon).

Both are smooth strictly positive, and

B_{k,epsilon}^n=n k^m b_epsilon A_epsilon^m∧w=C mu,
C=n k^m/H_epsilon.

For ANY smooth positive Gauduchon gamma, dd^c gamma^m=0. Stokes gives equality of the integrated pairings of Theta and B. Matrix AM–GM gives pointwise

B∧gamma^m=(tr(gamma^(-1)B)/n)gamma^n
≥(B^n/gamma^n)^(1/n)gamma^n
=C^(1/n)(mu/gamma^n)^(1/n)gamma^n.

Thus the defining quotient is at least C^(1/n) for every participating Gauduchon metric; no restriction to invariant or product tests has been made.

For actual attainment define

gamma_{k,epsilon}=b_epsilon^(-1/m)B_{k,epsilon}.

It is a global smooth positive metric, and

gamma_{k,epsilon}^m=b_epsilon^(-1)k^m A_epsilon^m+m k^{m-1}A_epsilon^{m-1}∧w.

The first term is pulled back from a top-degree base form and therefore d-closed; the second is a product of closed forms. Hence gamma is Gauduchon, in fact balanced. It is conformal to B, so AM–GM is an equality. Directly,

gamma^n=C b_epsilon^(-n/m)mu,
∫Theta∧gamma^m=C∫b_epsilon^(-1)mu=C H_epsilon=n k^m,
D_mu(gamma)=C^(m/n)H_epsilon.

The quotient is C^(1/n), proving

lambda_mu(Theta_{k,epsilon})^n=n k^m/H_epsilon.

For k=1 this gives all stated theta_epsilon formulas and actual smooth minimizing metrics. For k=1+epsilon it gives the exact Hermitian regularization value

lambda_mu(theta+epsilon h)^n=n(1+epsilon)^m/H_epsilon,

which decreases to n as epsilon decreases to zero.

The literal endpoint all-test infimum agrees. The positive current B_0=A+a w equals theta+dd^c phi. For every smooth positive Gauduchon gamma, Stokes and positivity give

∫theta∧gamma^m=∫B_0∧gamma^m
≥∫_{X\({p}×P^1)}B_0∧gamma^m
≥n^(1/n)D_mu(gamma).

On this complement, B_0 is smooth positive and B_0^n=n mu, so the preceding matrix inequality applies. The omitted fiber has zero mass for the smooth density appearing in D_mu. B_0∧gamma^m is a well-defined positive measure: it is a current wedged with a smooth form. No undefined singular determinant is used. Conversely theta≤theta_epsilon implies lambda_mu(theta)≤lambda_mu(theta_epsilon)=(n/H_epsilon)^(1/n). Taking epsilon↓0 proves

lambda_mu(theta)=n^(1/n), V_mu(theta)=n.

This is also the value obtained by the required decreasing Hermitian regularization. No smooth endpoint attaining metric is used or claimed.

Diagnostic evidence and limitations. checks.py symbolically verifies the radial eigenvalues and beta/x determinant. For m=2 it independently verifies phi(x)=2log(1+sqrt(x)). It compares H quadrature with the polynomial-division expression

H_epsilon=m beta[Σ_{j=0}^{m-2}(-c)^j/(m-1-j)+(-c)^(m-1)log((1+c)/c)], c=beta epsilon,

and checks the radial density using numerical differentiation. The successful run covers m=2,3,4,5,8,12 and epsilon=1,0.1,10^(-6): 18 parameter pairs, 54 pointwise density checks, and both minimizing quotient formulas. Its output reports PASS and maximum checked absolute algebra/quadrature error 3.4121697×10^(-39). For m=2, epsilon=1 it reports H=0.450693855665945154, V(theta_epsilon)=6.65640314880086523, and V(theta+epsilon h)=26.6256125952034609.

An initial unsplit 50-digit quadrature differed from the exact polynomial expression by about 5.06×10^(-33) at m=5, epsilon=10^(-6), exceeding the chosen tolerance. A single split still differed by 2.36×10^(-33); geometric splits at c,10c,100c,… resolved the numerical issue. The failure history is retained in checks.first.out and sources/check_history.txt. These are finite diagnostic observations, not exhaustive verification or substitutes for the proof valid for every m≥2.

notes.text:
Actual finite-time flow and its exact endpoint: target B.

Use the construction independently proved in n2. The initial metric

omega0=(n+1)omega+(a+2)w

is global smooth strictly positive, since n+1>0 and a+2≥2.

Its determinant and normalized Ricci form are exact. The product expansion gives

omega0^n=n(n+1)^m(a+2)mu.

The affine Fubini–Study determinant on P^m is a constant times (1+|z|²)^(-m-1), so -dd^c log omega^m=(m+1)omega=n omega. On P^1 the corresponding form is 2w. Coordinate changes contribute only pluriharmonic logarithms. Consequently

Ric(omega0)=n omega+2w-dd^c log(a+2),
alpha_t=omega0-t Ric(omega0)
=(n+1-nt)omega+(a+2-2t)w+t dd^c log(a+2).

For every 0≤t<1 the global smooth potential -t log(a+2) gives

alpha_t+dd^c[-t log(a+2)]
=(n+1-nt)omega+(a+2-2t)w>0.

Its horizontal coefficient exceeds 1, and its vertical coefficient is at least 2(1-t)>0. At t=1,

alpha1=theta+dd^c log(a+2).

This is a smooth gauge equivalence. It shows nefness using the strictly positive representatives of theta+epsilon h. It also shows nonbigness: a strict alpha1 representative would give a strict theta representative by adding the smooth function log(a+2) to its genuine quasi-psh potential, contradicting n2. Smooth addition preserves the canonical quasi-psh representative.

For every t>1 there is no positive current representative, including one obtained from an arbitrary scalar distribution u. Suppose alpha_t+dd^c u were positive. For a smooth nonnegative base function chi, the strongly semipositive test chi omega^m is dd^c-closed, as established in n2. Distributional Stokes removes dd^c u. The horizontal dd^c log(a+2) term has zero wedge with omega^m. Thus

0≤∫_X(alpha_t+dd^c u)∧chi omega^m
=∫_{P^m}(a+2-2t)chi omega^m.

For t>1 the coefficient is negative on an open neighborhood of p. Choosing a nonzero chi supported there contradicts positivity. At t=1 a semipositive representative exists, but no smooth strictly positive representative can exist: compactness would make it at least delta h and contradict nonbigness. These arguments establish both directions of the positivity-time criterion, without restricting singular potentials.

Source time conversion. The permitted foundation in n1 uses Ric_std=-i∂bar∂ log(det g), whereas this problem uses dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂. Therefore

Ric_std=2π Ric_original.

There is no metric rescaling. If omega_std(s) is its solution, omega(t)=omega_std(t/(2π)) satisfies

∂_t omega=-(1/(2π))Ric_std(omega)=-Ric_original(omega).

Thus t_original=2π s_std. The standard background at s is alpha_{2πs}, and i∂bar∂psi=dd^c(2πpsi). Hence existence of a smooth strict representative is exactly the condition already proved, with the entire potential class preserved.

The supplied maximal-time theorem consequently gives S=1/(2π) in standard time: strict representatives exist at all smaller times, and no positive current representative exists at any larger time. omega(t)=alpha_t+dd^c u_t,

The lower existence assertion is exactly the step using the permitted maximal-time theorem; no additional parabolic theorem is invoked.

Finally, for every smooth Gauduchon gamma, Stokes for the smooth function log(a+2) gives

∫alpha1∧gamma^m=∫theta∧gamma^m.

The same holds after adding epsilon h. Therefore both the full infimum and its decreasing regularization are gauge invariant here. By n2,

lambda_mu(alpha1)=n^(1/n), V_mu(alpha1)=n>0.

The actual limiting background theta_tau=omega0-tau Ric(omega0)=alpha1 is nef and nonbig. This proves every target B.

The explicit closed annihilator and every annihilator of this endpoint: targets C and D2.

Retain the construction and actual endpoint proved in n2 and n3. Let Z={p}×P^1. Its integration current [Z] has bidegree (n-1,n-1), is positive, and is d-closed by Stokes on the compact smooth complex curve. Hence dd^c[Z]=0.

Only smooth restrictions are used for normalization. Horizontal omega and dd^c log(a+2) restrict to zero on Z, and a(p)=0. Therefore

omega0|Z=2w, theta|Z=0, alpha1|Z=0.

The final equality uses the smooth formula alpha1=omega+a w+dd^c log(a+2), without restricting phi, A, or a singular current. Thus T=[Z]/2 satisfies

∫omega0∧T=1, ∫alpha1∧T=0, dd^c T=0.

Its trace sigma=omega0∧T is the probability measure w on Z, with support exactly Z.

Radon matrix convention. For a positive (n-1,n-1) current, local coefficients form a positive Hermitian matrix of measures. Positivity and polarization bound off-diagonal coefficient measures by the diagonal trace; hence all coefficients are absolutely continuous with respect to sigma_T=omega0∧T. Their Radon–Nikodym derivatives give a measurable positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix P_T such that, for every smooth real (1,1) form eta,

eta∧T=(1/n)tr(B_eta P_T)sigma_T,

where B_eta is its matrix relative to omega0. Taking eta=omega0 gives tr P_T=n sigma_T-almost everywhere. This elementary measure construction patches under unitary frame changes and needs no smoothness or d-closedness of T.

For T=[Z]/2 choose an omega0-unitary frame on Z with last vector vertical. If b_vert is the corresponding diagonal entry of B_eta, then eta|Z=2b_vert w. Consequently eta∧T=b_vert sigma, and the prescribed trace formula gives

P_T=n Pi_vert.

Thus tr P_T=n, rank P_T=1, and det P_T=0 sigma-almost everywhere.

The fixed-density determinant measure in this convention can be written

Gamma0(T)=rho0^(1/n)(det P_T)^(1/n)sigma_T,
rho0=mu/omega0^n>0.

Its normalization agrees with D_mu: for a smooth current T=gamma^(n-1), writing G=B_gamma gives sigma_T=r omega0^n, r=tr(adj G)/n, and P_T=(adj G)/r. Hence

rho0^(1/n)(det P_T)^(1/n)sigma_T=(mu/gamma^n)^(1/n)gamma^n.

For our singular current no density of sigma relative to volume is divided out. Since det P_T=0 sigma-almost everywhere, Gamma0(T) is the zero measure. The conclusion also holds for any smooth finite positive determinant weight. Here rho0=1/[n(n+1)^m(a+2)] is smooth and finite on Z.

Now let T be ANY positive (n-1,n-1) current satisfying dd^c T=0, ∫omega0∧T=1, and ∫alpha1∧T=0. No smoothness, d-closedness, special support, or equality to [Z]/2 is assumed. Smooth gauge Stokes gives

∫theta∧T=∫alpha1∧T=0.

The horizontal/vertical splitting is omega0-orthogonal, and

B_theta=(1/(n+1))Pi_hor+(a/(a+2))Pi_vert.

(1/n)tr(B_theta P_T)≥ell.

Because theta∧T=0, ∫ell d sigma_T=0. On X\Z, a>0 and ell>0. The union of sets ell≥1/j covers that complement, proving sigma_T(X\Z)=0. The trace probability is supported on the particular analytic fiber Z. This support conclusion comes from the smooth form’s zero set, not determinant vanishing.

On Z, B_theta=(1/(n+1))Pi_hor. Thus tr(Pi_hor P_T)=0 sigma_T-almost everywhere. Horizontal diagonal entries are nonnegative and sum to zero, so each vanishes. For a positive semidefinite matrix, |P_ij|²≤P_ii P_jj; therefore every row and column involving a horizontal entry vanishes. Only the vertical entry remains, and trace normalization makes it n. Hence every normalized annihilator satisfies

P_T=n Pi_vert, rank P_T=1, det P_T=0, Gamma0(T)=0

sigma_T-almost everywhere.
